reading.body:
Diffit is a teacher-facing AI tool that generates leveled readings, summaries, and questions, and its vendor states it collects no student data.

The product sits in a specific niche: adapting a source text or topic into material at different reading levels. That is a text transformation task, not a tutoring or assessment task, and the stated user is the teacher rather than the student. The privacy posture follows from that design. A tool that never touches student records has little to comply with under FERPA and COPPA, and the vendor's claims of compliance and no data sales are consistent with a product that only ever sees teacher input.

For AI scaling, the relevant fact is what the data does not contain. There is no model, no training run, no inference volume, no compute provider, and no data center or power figure anywhere in this record. A tool of this kind runs on hosted inference, but nothing here says at what scale, on whose hardware, or at what energy cost. The pricing model, a free tier with a 60 day premium trial and site licenses priced by enrollment, describes how schools buy it, not how much compute it consumes.

What the data does cover is narrow and should be read that way. It establishes one company, one product, one audience, and a set of vendor-stated privacy and pricing terms. It does not establish adoption, usage, effectiveness, or any link to the physical infrastructure that constrains AI. Any claim about Diffit's role in AI's compute buildout would have to come from outside this record.

profile_text.body:
Diffit is an AI tool that teachers use to generate instructional materials. According to its website, it produces leveled readings, summaries, and questions from a topic or source text, with the aim of giving teachers "just right" materials and helping students access grade level content. The site describes the resources as flexible and curriculum-aligned, and says they suit ELL, SPED, intervention, and MTSS contexts. The company cites a survey of elementary and secondary Diffit users conducted with a third party evaluator, in which 2,517 teachers completed the survey.

Diffit's product is listed in the Education and Research AI category. Its stated audience is teachers, and the vendor says it does not collect student data, states FERPA and COPPA compliance, and says it never sells data. Pricing includes a free version for teachers with a 60 day premium trial, and school site licenses priced by enrollment.

The available material does not include litigation, regulatory filings, or other outside records for Diffit.
